summary.one_liner: XAgent is an open-source experimental LLM-driven autonomous agent from OpenBMB that aims to automatically solve a wide range of tasks.
summary.what_it_does: XAgent is a general-purpose autonomous agent built around a Dispatcher (assigns tasks to agents), a Planner (splits tasks into subtasks with milestones and revises plans), and an Actor (uses tools to carry out subtasks and can ask humans for help). Actions run inside ToolServer, a Docker container that provides a File Editor, a Python Notebook, a Web Browser, a Shell, and a Rapid API tool for calling APIs from ToolBench's collection. The README says new tools can be added to ToolServer. Runs can be started from the command line with run.py and a config file, or through a web GUI served by nginx on port 5173. Each run saves a local workspace, a copy of the ToolServer workspace, and intermediate records such as LLM inputs and outputs, with API keys removed so records can be shared or replayed. The README describes the required model setup as OpenAI keys, recommending gpt-4-32k with a gpt-3.5-turbo-16k backup.
use_cases: Running autonomous web research and reporting
Writing and debugging code in a sandboxed container
Training and evaluating machine learning models
Getting restaurant or life-assistant recommendations with human input
how_to_run: docker compose build && docker compose up  (build ToolServer image from local sources)
Edit assets/config.yml to add at least one OpenAI API key
Open the web GUI on port 5173 (default login guest / xagent)
notable: Dual-loop Planner and Actor design that splits tasks into subtasks and milestones
Runs all actions inside a Docker container (ToolServer) for safety
Can ask the human for help mid-task via an AskForHumanHelp tool
Saves full run records with sensitive data removed for reproduction and sharing
Includes a web GUI as well as a command-line interface
caveats: README describes XAgent as experimental and in early stages
Requires Docker and Docker Compose plus at least one paid OpenAI API key
The README says gpt-3.5-turbo is not tested or recommended due to short context length
The README lists a Benchmarks section but gives no benchmark results
